description:
`graph export` drops in-scope issues and can return an empty graph for a valid `--scope`. Its node order also changes between runs over the same repository.

## Background

The dot, mermaid and JSON exporters gather nodes with `collect_all_nodes` (`crates/jit/src/visualization.rs:341-357`). It walks dependents from `graph.get_roots()`, the nodes whose `dependencies` list is empty. A scoped export builds the graph from the scope members only, but each member keeps its full dependency list. A member whose dependencies all lie outside the scope is not a root, so it and everything reachable only through it are skipped. When no member has an empty dependency list, the export is empty.

`get_roots` and `get_dependents` iterate the graph's `HashMap` (`crates/jit/src/graph/mod.rs:69, 260-275`), so the output order follows per-process hash seeding.

Reproduction:

```sh
jit init
X=<create "Outside">; T=<create "Task">; E=<create "Epic">
jit dep add $T $X; jit dep add $E $T
jit graph export --scope $E --json
# {"nodes": [], "edges": []}
# five unscoped exports of five independent issues: five different orders
```

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every format of a scoped export lists exactly the scope's member issues, including members whose dependencies all lie outside the scope.
- [hard] REQ-02: An unscoped export lists every issue in the repository.
- [hard] REQ-03: Repeated exports of an unchanged repository produce byte-identical output in every format.
- [hard] REQ-04: A regression test exports a scope whose members all depend on out-of-scope issues and asserts that every member appears.
- [hard] REQ-05: A property-based test over generated DAGs and scopes asserts that the exported node set equals the selected node set.

## Notes

The exporters already receive the selected node set, so collection needs no traversal. Iterating the graph's nodes in a deterministic order (for example by ID) satisfies REQ-01 to REQ-03.
title: Graph export lists every in-scope issue in a stable order
